claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has a complex and unstable thermal response upon reheating.
Replacing approximately 5 at% phosphorus with boron will improve glass-forming ability during rapid solidification.
Replacing approximately 5 at% phosphorus with boron will enhance amorphous-phase thermal stability during reheating.
Boron substitution enhances atomic packing in the alloy.
Boron substitution improves short-range chemical order while increasing local disorder.
Short-range chemical order can arise at the solidification front of multi-principal-element alloys even at extreme cooling rates.
Boron perturbs short-range order at the solidification front.
Boron acts as a network former in the amorphous matrix.
Boron increases atomic-size mismatch in the alloy.
The boron-induced structural changes raise the energy barrier for crystallization during solidification and reheating.
The increased crystallization barrier suppresses nucleation of competing crystalline phases.
Boron substitution will broaden the cooling-rate window over which an amorphous phase forms.
Boron substitution will increase the crystallization-onset temperature by several tens of degrees Celsius relative to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The intervention is expected to operate under cooling rates of approximately 10^2 to 10^3 K/s.
Cooling significantly below approximately 10^2 K/s may prevent the proposed improvement in amorphous retention and thermal stability.
Boron additions exceeding approximately 5 at% may cause phase segregation or boron-rich compound formation.
The optimal boron concentration and its interaction with phosphorus are not yet established.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator says boron improves short-range chemical order, whereas the mechanism says it perturbs short-range order and increases disorder. The hypothesis does not distinguish chemical short-range order from other forms of local disorder, leaving these descriptions in unresolved tension.
